0.en: Lena didn't need to be asked twice. She pulled the western road camera onto the station's big monitor and dragged the timeline back to dawn.
0.id: Lena tidak perlu diminta dua kali. Ia menarik tayangan kamera jalan barat ke monitor besar stasiun dan menyeret lini waktunya mundur ke subuh.

2.en: Sarah leaned forward in her chair.

3.en: Half past six. When the light first hit the grass.
3.id: Setengah tujuh. Waktu cahaya pertama kali mengenai rumput.

4.en: The image jumped. Gray light, the white maintenance cart at the end of the road, and beyond it the wall of stems. At first Jack didn't see anything different.
4.id: Gambarnya melompat. Cahaya kelabu, kereta pemeliharaan putih di ujung jalan, dan di baliknya dinding batang rumput. Awalnya Jack tidak melihat ada yang berbeda.

5.en: Then the sun came up behind the camera, and the grass caught fire.
5.id: Lalu matahari terbit di belakang kamera, dan rumput itu seakan terbakar.

6.en: Every blade was hung with water. Beads of it clung along the edges of the leaves and gathered at the tips, round and heavy and shining, some no bigger than a fist, some as tall as a man's chest. The low sun passed straight through them, and the whole wall of grass lit up like a chandelier.
6.id: Setiap helai digantungi air. Butir-butirnya menempel di sepanjang tepi daun dan berkumpul di ujung-ujungnya, bulat dan berat dan berkilauan, ada yang tak lebih besar dari kepalan tangan, ada yang setinggi dada orang dewasa. Matahari yang masih rendah menembus langsung butir-butir itu, dan seluruh dinding rumput menyala seperti lampu gantung kristal.

7.en: Mark let out a long, low whistle.

8.en: Lena let it play forward. As the light rose, the beads shrank. They didn't fall. They simply grew smaller and smaller, like they were being breathed in, until by nine o'clock the grass was dry and green and ordinary again.
8.id: Lena memutarnya maju. Saat cahaya naik, butir-butir itu menyusut. Tidak jatuh. Hanya makin lama makin kecil, seperti sedang dihirup, sampai pada pukul sembilan rumput itu kering dan hijau dan biasa lagi.

10.en: Every morning. That's there every morning.
10.id: Setiap pagi. Itu ada di sana setiap pagi.

11.en: Jack stared at the frozen frame Lena had stopped on, six-forty, the light right through the biggest drops.
11.id: Jack menatap gambar beku tempat Lena menghentikan rekaman, pukul enam empat puluh, cahaya tepat menembus tetesan-tetesan terbesar.

13.en: He's on his way over with Unit Four. Paul's crew is at the greenhouse measuring for the new line, and Aiden didn't trust them not to drown his seedlings.
13.id: Dia sedang ke sini bersama Unit Empat. Kru Paul ada di rumah kaca mengukur untuk jalur baru, dan Aiden tidak percaya mereka tidak akan menenggelamkan bibitnya.

14.en: Aiden arrived ten minutes later, out of breath and still slightly muddy. He looked at the screen, and his face changed completely. For the first time all day, he didn't look frightened. He looked interested.
14.id: Aiden tiba sepuluh menit kemudian, terengah-engah dan masih agak berlumpur. Ia melihat layar, dan wajahnya berubah total. Untuk pertama kalinya hari itu, ia tidak tampak takut. Ia tampak tertarik.

15.en: Oh. That's dew. Some of it. And guttation.
15.id: Oh. Itu embun. Sebagian. Dan gutasi.

18.en: Guttation. At night, plants push extra water up through their roots, and it comes out at the tips of the leaves. Those big ones at the ends, those are the plant's own water. The little ones along the edges are dew from the air.
18.id: Gutasi. Di malam hari, tanaman mendorong kelebihan air naik lewat akarnya, dan air itu keluar di ujung-ujung daun. Yang besar-besar di ujung itu air tanaman itu sendiri. Yang kecil-kecil di sepanjang tepi itu embun dari udara.

21.en: The dew's basically clean. The guttation drops have minerals and sugars in them. You'd want to test it. Filter it, at least.
21.id: Embunnya pada dasarnya bersih. Tetesan gutasi mengandung mineral dan gula. Sebaiknya diuji dulu. Setidaknya disaring.

23.en: And you'd want to be very careful getting it.

26.en: Aiden pointed at the biggest drop on the screen.
26.id: Aiden menunjuk tetesan terbesar di layar.

27.en: Because insects drown in it. All the time. In the greenhouse, I find gnats stuck in drops on the leaves every morning. The water grabs them, and they can't push their way back out. That one comes up past your chest. If you fell into it, I'm not sure you'd get out either.
27.id: Karena serangga tenggelam di dalamnya. Sering sekali. Di rumah kaca, setiap pagi aku menemukan agas terjebak di tetesan air di daun. Airnya mencengkeram mereka, dan mereka tidak bisa mendorong diri keluar lagi. Yang itu tingginya lewat dada. Kalau kamu jatuh ke dalamnya, aku tidak yakin kamu juga bisa keluar.

28.en: Nobody said anything for a moment.
28.id: Sesaat tak ada yang berkata apa-apa.

29.en: Jack did the math in his head, then did it again on Lena's tablet because he didn't trust himself on no sleep.
29.id: Jack menghitung di kepala, lalu menghitungnya lagi di tablet Lena karena ia tidak percaya pada dirinya sendiri yang belum tidur.

30.en: Call that one most of a meter across. Even if I'm generous with the shape, it holds more than two hundred liters.
30.id: Anggap saja yang itu lebarnya hampir satu meter. Bahkan kalau aku murah hati soal bentuknya, isinya lebih dari dua ratus liter.

33.en: One drop. That's ten people's water for a day. And that screen was covered in them.
33.id: Satu tetes. Itu jatah air sepuluh orang untuk sehari. Dan layar itu penuh dengan tetesan seperti itu.

34.en: Sarah had her hand pressed flat against her stomach, the way she did when she was thinking hard.
34.id: Sarah menekankan telapak tangannya rata ke perutnya, seperti biasa kalau ia sedang berpikir keras.

35.en: So we have three weeks of water in the tanks, and more water than we could ever use sitting just past the end of the road every morning.
35.id: Jadi kita punya air untuk tiga minggu di tangki, dan air yang lebih banyak daripada yang bisa kita pakai tersedia tepat di balik ujung jalan setiap pagi.

36.en: Mark pushed himself off the doorframe.
36.id: Mark mendorong tubuhnya menjauh dari kusen pintu.

37.en: Sitting past the end of the road, inside a forest full of things the size of cars. This morning I told that kid nobody even walks to the end of the road. You told the whole town nobody goes past it. Now you're going to stand there and tell me we're going out?
37.id: Tersedia di balik ujung jalan, di dalam hutan yang penuh makhluk sebesar mobil. Pagi ini aku bilang ke anak itu bahwa tidak ada yang boleh jalan ke ujung jalan sekalipun. Kamu bilang ke seluruh kota tidak ada yang melewatinya. Sekarang kamu mau berdiri di situ dan bilang ke aku kita akan keluar?

40.en: Jack looked at the frozen frame again. The light through the water. Two hundred liters in a single drop, and the jumping spider somewhere in that same grass, warming up, waiting for something fast enough to look like food.
40.id: Jack memandang gambar beku itu lagi. Cahaya yang menembus air. Dua ratus liter dalam satu tetes, dan laba-laba pelompat itu di suatu tempat di rumput yang sama, sedang menghangatkan diri, menunggu sesuatu yang cukup cepat untuk tampak seperti makanan.

41.en: Not tomorrow, either. This morning we ran in because we didn't have a choice. This time we plan it.
41.id: Besok juga tidak. Pagi ini kita bergegas masuk karena tidak punya pilihan. Kali ini kita merencanakannya.

43.en: A small team. Roped together. On radio, every two minutes, the way you and I did last night. The very edge of the western road and no farther.
43.id: Tim kecil. Diikat tali satu sama lain. Lapor lewat radio tiap dua menit, seperti yang kamu dan aku lakukan semalam. Sampai ujung paling akhir jalan barat dan tidak lebih jauh.

45.en: One jug. And a sample for Aiden to test. That's all. If it works once, we know how to do it again.
45.id: Satu jeriken. Dan satu sampel untuk diuji Aiden. Itu saja. Kalau berhasil sekali, kita tahu cara melakukannya lagi.

48.en: First light. When the water's there and the spider's still cold. Back before the sun's off the grass. Nine o'clock at the latest.
48.id: Saat cahaya pertama. Waktu airnya ada dan laba-labanya masih kedinginan. Kembali sebelum matahari lepas dari rumput. Paling lambat jam sembilan.

49.en: And if the spider's not cold?

50.en: Then we stand very still and try not to look like flies.
50.id: Kalau begitu kita berdiri diam sekali dan berusaha tidak kelihatan seperti lalat.

51.id: Kamu sudah bilang itu tadi pagi.

53.en: Mark didn't laugh. But he didn't say no, either.
53.id: Mark tidak tertawa. Tapi ia juga tidak bilang tidak.

54.en: The day after tomorrow. I want a whole day to plan it. I want to know every single thing that can go wrong before I let anyone stand next to one of those.
54.id: Lusa. Aku mau satu hari penuh untuk merencanakannya. Aku mau tahu setiap hal yang bisa salah sebelum aku membiarkan siapa pun berdiri di samping salah satu tetesan itu.

56.en: Aiden had gone very quiet. He was looking at the screen as though it had asked him a question.
56.id: Aiden jadi sangat diam. Ia memandang layar seolah layar itu baru saja mengajukan pertanyaan kepadanya.

57.en: I could tell you which plants those are. The ones with the biggest drops. If I could see them up close.
57.id: Aku bisa memberi tahu kalian tanaman apa itu. Yang tetesannya paling besar. Kalau aku bisa melihatnya dari dekat.

58.en: Jack heard what he wasn't saying.
58.id: Jack mendengar apa yang tidak ia ucapkan.

61.en: I want to not be useless.
61.id: Aku mau tidak jadi orang yang tidak berguna.

62.en: Sarah looked at him for a long moment, the way she looked at an experiment she hadn't decided about yet.
62.id: Sarah memandangnya lama, seperti caranya memandang eksperimen yang belum ia putuskan.

63.en: You weren't useless this morning. You knew what it was. Nobody else did.
63.id: Kamu tidak tidak berguna tadi pagi. Kamu tahu makhluk apa itu. Tidak ada orang lain yang tahu.

64.en: Paul's voice crackled over Lena's radio before anybody could decide anything.
64.id: Suara Paul berderak lewat radio Lena sebelum ada yang sempat memutuskan apa pun.

65.en: Measured the greenhouse end. I'll have treated water on those plants by tonight. Tell the kid his tomatoes will live.
65.id: Ujung rumah kaca sudah diukur. Malam ini tanaman-tanaman itu sudah dapat air olahan. Bilang ke anak itu tomatnya bakal selamat.

66.en: Aiden let out a breath that was half a laugh.
66.id: Aiden mengembuskan napas yang setengahnya tawa.

69.en: Don't thank me. Put my coolant on the list.
69.id: Jangan berterima kasih. Masukkan cairan pendingin saya ke daftar.

73.en: The afternoon went the way afternoons go when nobody has slept. Jack answered calls. Sarah, in her chair, answered more of them than he did, and twice Mark had to remind her that her five minutes of arguing were up. Lena posted the first supply window for the evening. Somewhere in the middle of it all, Jack fell asleep sitting upright against a warm pipe and woke an hour later with Sarah's jacket over him and no memory of either.
73.id: Sore itu berjalan seperti sore mana pun ketika tak ada yang sempat tidur. Jack menjawab telepon. Sarah, dari kursinya, menjawab lebih banyak lagi, dan dua kali Mark harus mengingatkannya bahwa jatah lima menit berdebatnya sudah habis. Lena mengumumkan sesi pasokan pertama untuk malam itu. Di tengah semua itu, Jack tertidur sambil duduk tegak bersandar ke pipa yang hangat dan terbangun sejam kemudian dengan jaket Sarah menyelimutinya, tanpa ingatan soal keduanya.

74.en: It was nearly dark when Mark finally drove them home.
74.id: Hari sudah hampir gelap ketika Mark akhirnya mengantar mereka pulang.

75.en: The house was exactly as they had left it, the night before, when this had all been an ordinary late shift. Two coffee mugs in the sink. A baby blanket folded on the arm of the couch, still waiting for a crib that wasn't built yet. Jack stood in the doorway and looked at it all for a long moment, as though he were seeing somebody else's home.
75.id: Rumah itu persis seperti ketika mereka tinggalkan, malam sebelumnya, ketika semua ini masih sekadar sif malam biasa. Dua cangkir kopi di bak cuci. Selimut bayi terlipat di lengan sofa, masih menunggu boks bayi yang belum dirakit. Jack berdiri di ambang pintu dan memandangi semuanya lama, seolah sedang melihat rumah orang lain.

76.en: Doctor Mercer came at eight, as promised, and wrapped the cuff around Sarah's arm in the kitchen. She watched the numbers settle.
76.id: Dokter Mercer datang pukul delapan, sesuai janji, dan melilitkan manset di lengan Sarah di dapur. Ia memperhatikan angka-angkanya menetap.

79.en: I said better, not good. Still a little high. I'll be back tomorrow night. Until then, rest. Real rest. Not chair rest.
79.id: Saya bilang lebih baik, bukan bagus. Masih agak tinggi. Saya kembali besok malam. Sampai saat itu, istirahat. Istirahat sungguhan. Bukan istirahat di kursi.

81.en: You ran a water department from a chair.
81.id: Anda menjalankan departemen air dari kursi.

82.en: Sarah didn't argue with that, which was how Jack knew how tired she was.
82.id: Sarah tidak membantahnya, dan dari situlah Jack tahu betapa lelahnya ia.

83.en: After the doctor had gone, they sat on the couch in the dark with the outward-facing lights switched off, the way everyone along the edge had been asked to. Through the window, past the rooftops, the grass stood black against a sky full of stars.
83.id: Setelah dokter itu pergi, mereka duduk di sofa dalam gelap dengan lampu-lampu yang menghadap ke luar dimatikan, seperti yang diminta dari semua orang di sepanjang tepian. Lewat jendela, melewati atap-atap, rumput berdiri hitam berlatar langit penuh bintang.

86.en: It wasn't a question, so he didn't answer it like one.
86.id: Itu bukan pertanyaan, jadi Jack tidak menjawabnya seperti pertanyaan.

87.en: To the end of the road. Not one step farther.
87.id: Sampai ujung jalan. Tidak selangkah pun lebih jauh.

88.en: You said that about the boundary last night.
88.id: Kamu bilang begitu soal batas itu semalam.

90.en: With a fingernail story and a cut hand.
90.id: Dengan cerita potongan kuku dan tangan yang luka.

91.en: Four stitches. Mercer was very proud of them.
91.id: Empat jahitan. Mercer bangga sekali dengan jahitannya.

92.en: She was quiet for a while. Then she took his good hand and pressed it flat against her stomach, and after a moment something on the other side pushed back, firm and annoyed and very much alive.
92.id: Sarah diam beberapa lama. Lalu ia meraih tangan Jack yang tidak terluka dan menekankannya rata ke perutnya, dan sesaat kemudian sesuatu di sisi lain mendorong balik, kuat dan sebal dan sungguh-sungguh hidup.

93.en: He wants you to come back by nine.
93.id: Dia mau kamu kembali sebelum jam sembilan.

95.en: You tell him. He heard your voice on every speaker in town this morning. He'll recognize it.
95.id: Kamu yang bilang. Tadi pagi dia mendengar suaramu di setiap pengeras suara di kota. Dia pasti mengenalinya.

96.en: Jack bent his head, close, and said it quietly enough that only the two of them would hear.
96.id: Jack menundukkan kepala, dekat, dan mengucapkannya cukup pelan sampai hanya mereka berdua yang mendengar.

97.en: He thought about the hall. Sixty faces, and nearly five hundred more behind the speakers. One of them, maybe, had sat and listened to him promise to find them.
97.id: Ia teringat aula itu. Enam puluh wajah, dan hampir lima ratus lagi di balik pengeras suara. Salah satu dari mereka, mungkin, sudah duduk dan mendengarkannya berjanji akan menemukan orang itu.

98.en: Far out past the edge of town, something heavy came down in the grass, once, and then the night was still again.
98.id: Jauh di luar tepian kota, sesuatu yang berat mendarat di rumput, sekali, lalu malam kembali hening.

99.en: Neither of them moved. After a while, Sarah's breathing slowed, and her hand went loose over his, and Jack sat in the dark and listened to the island and didn't sleep at all.
99.id: Tak satu pun dari mereka bergerak. Beberapa saat kemudian, napas Sarah melambat, dan tangannya terkulai lemas di atas tangan Jack, dan Jack duduk dalam gelap mendengarkan pulau itu dan sama sekali tidak tidur.
